story_text.value:
Hi HN community,

This is Salvador Faria. I've build a platform that allow mid/large organizations to get a view of their digital ecosystem and make informed decisions about their digital properties.

The platform tries to makes things easier for the end users:

- find all company sites

- grades all sites on key categories (end result is a site report)

- "Fix with AI" feature creates fixes for the issues found

Some technical aspects:

- Built with python/django/nextjs/postgres/gcp

- Each page is graded using custom audits and common Google Lighthouse audits

- AI is used to remove false positives (eg: typos)

You can access it from: https://weblidar.com

About me: I've been working in the web development space for some time, and I have built a similar platform for a large company in the past.

story_text.value:
Hi HN,

I've worked with React Native for years, but I've never been fully satisfied with it. That's why I'm building Hozo, an open-source UI compiler written in Rust.

In short, Hozo is yet another cross-platform UI framework like React Native Web, Tamagui, React Strict DOM, and Lynx.

The idea is to share source code, not necessarily runtime abstractions. For example, a Heading compiles to an h2 on the web and a Text with the header role on iOS and Android.

* Web: Semantic HTML and CSS without react-native-web.

* Mobile: Standard React Native components and precomputed StyleSheets.

* Styling: Tailwind CSS and StyleX with CSS-like text inheritance on React Native.

* A11y: First-class support with platform-specific semantics and compile-time ARIA validation.

* Guardrails: Compile-time diagnostics for both humans and AI agents.

Hozo supports SVG, 2D Canvas, Three.js, and WebView. It works with Vite, Next.js, Astro (including zero-JS static components), Metro/Expo, TanStack Start, Tauri, and Storybook. There's also a component library with an optional shadcn mode, and migration tooling for existing RN projects.

It's still early, though. I'm curious what others think of Hozo.

Docs: https://iray-tno.github.io/hozo/docs/

title.value: Show HN: Hozo compiles React Native to native UI and semantic HTML

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I'm Nathan. I wanted to share a project that I've been working on this month.

A few weeks ago, my Rust target folders had grown to about 70 GB across many git worktrees, and I asked Claude to figure out how to stop that from happening. It couldn't find much online, so we started to build our own workaround using some unstable cargo flags. Then someone on r/rust asked why we hadn't just used kache. Someone else mentioned Mr Boxington on a GitHub issue (another great solution).

I also got annoyed that my Claude Code sessions would constantly ask me to reauthenticate my MCP servers, which happens when you run a lot of them in parallel. An agent couldn't find any good "MCP proxy" so we started planning and building our own. I searched Google myself and found MCPProxy.app. It worked pretty well so I wrote a blog post and shared it on X. Some people replied and told me that Executor.sh was an even better solution. They were right, so I switched to Executor.

After all this, I decided to build Talira: A search engine for software that an AI agent can check before it starts building your own solution. You describe the problem in plain words ("my Rust target folders use 80 GB across git worktrees"). Talira searches the catalog using vector embeddings and uses Jev for filtering and reranking.

To try it:

- Search on https://talira.ai

- Add the MCP server to Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user talira https://mcp.talira.ai/mcp

Your agent can also send a report after each search: the problem in general terms, what you tried, what you kept and why. The idea is that it can eventually become a crowd-sourced database of tools that people actually chose and continued using over time.

It's currently in beta and the catalog still has a lot of gaps. I should also mention that I'm aware that ChatGPT and Claude already know a lot and are already very good at search. So there are plenty of cases where you don't need Talira at all. I'll need to collect some more real-world searches before I can benchmark it properly to see if it makes any difference.

I'd like to know if you've ever had any similar experiences. Let me know if an AI wasn't able to find a good solution that already existed.

Thanks for reading!

title.value: Show HN: Talira – Search engine for software, built for AI agents

story_text.value:
I was inspired by Mochi and Anki, but wanted to make something that’s a mix of the two. Anki is very confusing and has an outdated interface while Mochi is very simple and has a more minimalist interface. Olumino is the combination of both.

I also added Japanese flashcard support, including kana readings, for anyone learning the language.

I’m a CS student building this in my free time, so I’d love to hear what people think!
